$comment: What .github/scripts/release-notes.py needs to know that is true of this repo
and no other. The rules it applies - which label means which section, that an
unlabelled pull request never reaches Features - are the same across the suite
and live in the script, vendored from kollektiv. The paths below are Kommands'
own: Konnekt has website/ and agent_docs/, and a shared list would be wrong for
both. This file is also the adoption marker kollektiv's sync-notes.sh reads.
sets additionalProperties:false and its CI validates this repo's manifest
nightly, so a new key there is a change that has to land in kollektiv first.
This file has one consumer sitting next to it and needs no such coordination.
$nonAppPaths: Prefixes, matched against each changed file. A pull request touching only
these did not change the web app or the desktop build, so it is left out of
the notes and counted in the footer instead.
docs/ is read in the repo. .github/ is CI and release tooling; .claude/ and
.aislop/ are agent and gate configuration; scripts/ is tooling (the generators
write their output under src/data/generated, which is where a data change
shows up, so a generator-only pull request that regenerated nothing changed
nothing a user gets); the root files are repo furniture. eslint.config.js is
lint policy and never reaches the bundle.
Not listed, on purpose: build/ holds the app icon, the .desktop file and the
macOS plist, which ship with the desktop build. tokens.source.json is not
listed either: a token change ships once src/styles/tokens.css is
regenerated, and the generated-file check fails a pull request that refreshed
the source without regenerating. tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts, package.json
and wails.json are build config that does not ship, but excluding them by
path would also hide real app work in the same pull request; that case is
what the type:chore label is for.
